punchline: Britain's cycling team started winning when its coach began worrying about pillows, hand-washing and dust in the truck.
thirty_sec: In 2003, British Cycling had won a single Olympic gold since 1908. Their new performance director, Dave Brailsford, didn't look for one big fix. He looked for a 1 percent gain in everything: comfier seats, better tire grip, the right pillows, surgeon-taught hand-washing, even a white truck interior to spot dust. Five years later, at Beijing 2008, the team won roughly 60 percent of the cycling golds available.
question: If you could get just 1 percent better at one thing every day, what would you pick?
